name: Ibn Mālik
known: Jamāl al-Dīn Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ṭāʾī al-Jayyānī
summary: Andalusian grammarian who settled in Damascus; his thousand-verse Alfiyya became the most studied poem of Arabic grammar.
bio: Born in Jaén in al-Andalus, Ibn Mālik went east, studied in Aleppo with Ibn al-Ḥājib and Ibn Yaʿīsh, taught in Aleppo and Hama, and spent his most productive years in Damascus, where he died in 672/1274.
Beside the Alfiyya he wrote Tashīl al-fawāʾid on naḥw and Lāmiyyat al-afʿāl, a poem on the verb that is read in ṣarf. His son Badr al-Dīn wrote a commentary on the Alfiyya.
